correctness.rationale: The theorem is intrinsic to the zero-sum Euclidean hyperplane and uses unit edge generators. A facet normal of a connected graphical zonotope is a bond cut; distance is |∂S|sqrt(N/[k(N-k)])/2. The Laplacian of K_{p,q}, p<=q, has eigenvalues p (q-1), q (p-1), N,0 and gives |∂S|>=p k(N-k)/N. For N>=6 and 2<=k<=N-2, k(N-k)>=2(N-2)>N²/(N-1), excluding every nonsingleton cut strictly. N=5 uses explicit mixed cuts; K_{2,2} has mixed-cut distance 1, below singleton 2/sqrt3. Equality of antipodal supporting inequalities forces all degree-minimum singleton coordinates to zero and yields center dimensions p-1 or 0. For p=2<q, cuts with exactly one A-vertex give |t|<=q/2-sqrt((b+1)(q+1-b)/(q+1)); maximizing the quadratic yields the exact interval. For K_{2,2}, mixed cuts constrain t and singleton cuts give |t|<=1-sqrt3/2. Independent exact enumerator checked all 2,026 cut-size types in 44 p,q pairs; this does not prove the all-parameter inequalities.
